name: Mikaelinkirkko
observations: Red brick church with an asymmetrical entrance front: a very tall square bell tower on the left, a central gable, and a smaller pointed tower on the right.

The supplied height tag is 14.09 m, but its measurement reference is unspecified and the record explicitly describes estimated modelling. It is retained as uncertain body-height evidence, not interpreted as the full height of the church or main spire.

No physical dimensions are directly measured. Window dimensions have approximately 30 percent uncertainty; tower elevations approximately 35 percent. The main spire's total height is visually estimated at approximately 70–80 m.

The entrance facade has one large circular rose window within a pointed stone surround, above three pointed entrance arches and three small porch gables. The generic windows parameters describe the repeated side windows only.
Four large pointed window bays are clearly visible along the photographed side, each beneath a decorated transverse gable and separated by projecting stepped buttresses.
Side windows have pale stone surrounds and multiple slender vertical divisions. Three principal mullions are estimated; smaller glazing bars are additional.

The main tower has three tall louvred openings on the entrance-facing elevation, divided horizontally by a stone transom. The central pointed head rises above the outer two; opening_rows simplify these unequal heights into two groups on one face.
The main tower's brick shaft ends in steep gables with corner pinnacles around a much taller dark, tapering spire. Round turrets with conical roofs occur toward the opposite end.

Main roof slopes, spires and porch roofs visibly carry small overlapping grey slate-like units. Green patinated copper occurs chiefly on finials, spire tips, flashing, gutters and buttress caps; the supplied pale-green roof colour does not describe the dominant photographed roof surface.
Roof seam_m approximates the visible slate course spacing, not a standing-seam metal joint. Roof patina describes the dominant slate surface rather than the localized copper.
Stone appears chiefly in the low foundation, steps, window surrounds and decorative inserts. tower.stone_top_m describes the estimated foundation extent, not a stone tower stage.
No clock is visible on the photographed tower faces; clock_height_m and clock_radius_m are zero to represent absence.
Brick bond is provisionally running, with low confidence because individual headers are not consistently resolved. Brick and stone unit sizes are material-scale assumptions rather than measurements.
Colours estimate neutral material albedo after allowing for warm sunlight, blue skylight and shade. Material identification and facade arrangement are more reliable than absolute dimensions.
Survey calibration: city building103371568P base14.845m N2000, top90.186m; belfry wall width8.3m and top35.9m above base. Main spire total75.341m above base agrees with reference estimate.
